question: Which of the following dance forms belongs to the Vaishnava Monasteries of North East India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated in the **Vaishnava Monasteries of Assam** in North East India.
 
• Sattriya dance was introduced in the 15th century AD by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer **Sankardev**.
 
• It is traditionally performed in the **monasteries known as Sattras** as a part of the rituals and daily worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Odisha** in eastern India.
 
• It is known for its sensuous and lyrical nature, and the dance is characterized by various bhangas (stances), which involve stamping of the foot and striking various postures as seen in Indian sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**
 
 
• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from the state of **Kerala**.
 
• The term Mohiniattam comes from the words 'Mohini' meaning a woman who enchants onlookers and 'attam' meaning graceful and sensuous body movements.
 
• It is performed as a solo recital by women and is known for its graceful movements and feminine themes.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from the state of **Andhra Pradesh** in South India.
 
• It derives its name from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh and is known for its fast rhythms and fluid movements.
 
• The dance usually begins with an invocation followed by the nritta, nritya, and natya components.
